subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram Channel: Support Thread Binding for Subagent Sessions

question: Should Telegram expose explicit child-topic persistent subagent sessions now, and should that use the core SessionBindingService/channel capability path while preserving Telegram's current-conversation default?
rationale: Current main solves the old missing-adapter/hook infrastructure, but exposing child topics changes visible Telegram topic creation, delivery routing, session persistence, and plugin capability/API shape.

options.title: Review or replace the active Telegram PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 as the main design input, resolve conflicts and review findings, and require live Telegram proof on the final head.

options.title: Defer child-topic spawning
options.body: Keep current-conversation Telegram binding only until maintainers settle the default visibility and channel policy questions in the related issues.

options.title: Reject Telegram child-topic spawning
options.body: Close this feature direction and associated candidate PRs if maintainers decide internal subagent work should not create Telegram topics.

recommendation.title: Review or replace the active Telegram PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 as the main design input, resolve conflicts and review findings, and require live Telegram proof on the final head.

likelyOwner.reason: The current core adapter path and hook deprecation direction trace most directly to his merged refactor.
